description: One number, one duration, one timestamp -- written the same way by every runtime that writes it. A count rendered by a PowerShell command lands in a transcript; the same count rendered by a browser lands on the page above it; a Go service writes it into a report. A reader comparing those three has no way to tell a formatting difference from a real one, so the three agree here or one of them is wrong. The expected strings are the contract, not a recording of what any implementation currently happens to do.

cases.name: integer below the first group
cases.why: No separator appears until there is something to separate.

cases.name: integer at the first group boundary
cases.why: Exactly four digits is where an off-by-one in the grouping loop shows up.

cases.name: integer across several groups
the same integer in a locale that groups with a period
cases.why: pt-BR swaps both separators. A runtime reading its own locale database rather than the manifest is most visible here.

cases.name: zero
a negative integer keeps its sign outside the grouping
cases.why: Grouping from the right over a string that still carries the minus produces '-1,234,567' or '-,123,456,7' depending on where the sign was stripped.

cases.name: a decimal groups the whole part and not the fraction
the same decimal with the separators exchanged
a negative decimal
a decimal rounds to two places rather than truncating
an hour and a half floors to the hour
cases.why: The whole-hours part is where rounding is least likely to be questioned, and rounding up reports more time than actually passed.

cases.name: just under an hour stays in minutes
exactly an hour
a minute and a half
under a minute
zero duration
a duration does not change shape with the locale
cases.why: The hour and minute letters are English, and stay so until a catalog carries a translated duration pattern. What must not happen is one runtime translating them while another does not.

cases.name: a timestamp is written in UTC in a fixed shape
cases.why: A timestamp read off a page and pasted into a transcript search has to be the string the transcript holds, in every locale.

cases.name: the same timestamp in another locale
an external string is placed exactly as given
cases.why: Third-party text is shown and never parsed back into state, so no runtime may trim, case-fold or re-encode it.
